overall: Tomorrow, Wednesday June 25, Atlanta should see a mostly sunny day with light east winds of 0–5 mph and no precipitation risk — a classic early Atlanta summer day. No significant weather hazards affect the metro area; the patchy fog alert is limited to far north Georgia and has already lifted, while the flood warnings involve rivers in south Georgia well away from Atlanta.
forecast_obs_notes: Most models cluster tightly in the upper 80s: ECMWF (88.1°F), HRRR (89.5°F), NBM (87.0°F), and Weather.com (87.3°F) show strong agreement. GFS is a clear outlier at 77.4°F, which drags the forecast-only model down to 83.4°F, but the full ensemble — anchored by today's observed high of 69.8°F — corrects for this and places the expected TMAX at 87.2°F, closely matching the NWS narrative forecast of 'near 87.'
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model projects a TMAX of 87.2°F, in tight agreement with the NWS point forecast of near 87°F and the NBM/Weather.com consensus. The even bucket set modal peak at 90–91°F (51.6%) introduces some upside risk toward the low 90s, but the probability-weighted expected value and the majority of independent model guidance anchor the best estimate solidly in the upper 80s. Overall confidence is moderate-to-good (Tier 2, ~52% expected accuracy on the even bucket set), with the primary uncertainty being whether the slight ECMWF/HRRR warm bias materializes or the GFS cooler solution has any validity.
